shots.prompt: Establishing shot of a lantern-lit harbor square at dusk, circus wagons rattling over the cobbles past moored fishing boats; the ringmaster rides on the first wagon, lifting his top hat to the gulls.
Medium shot of the ringmaster shouting instructions through a brass megaphone, glancing nervously at storm clouds piling up over the sea.
The stagehand quietly backs a wagon into place while gusts tug at the striped canvas around him.
The ringmaster climbs onto a barrel and gives a booming speech to the performers sheltering under a market awning.
The stagehand kneels beside a tangle of guy ropes, picking at the knots with a bored look while the wind howls.
Wide view of lightning flickering over the open sea as fishermen haul their boats higher up the slipway.
The ringmaster hides behind a stack of crates and peeks out with theatrical caution as a loose tarpaulin flaps past overhead.
A sudden gust lifts the half-raised big top off its poles and drops it in a tidy heap of canvas on the empty pier.
The ringmaster smooths his tailcoat and marches over to the fallen tent, behaving as if the whole thing was rehearsed.
The stagehand waves the townsfolk toward the pier, carrying a coil of rope on his shoulder.
The ringmaster strolls along a row of tired performers wringing out their costumes, giving each a grand bow that hides his relief.
The stagehand passes the ringmaster a chipped enamel cup of cocoa without a word, still watching the clouds as the lanterns sway.
The ringmaster sips the cocoa, winces at the heat, then tips his hat to a fishing crew heading home.
A long line of townsfolk under umbrellas files along the harbor wall, outlined against the last light over the water.
The ringmaster gazes at the sagging tent, a flash of worry crossing his face before the showman's grin returns.
The stagehand coils the last rope and trails the ringmaster back toward the wagons, as unimpressed as ever.
A hand-painted closing card over the harbor at night carries one dry line about the show going on.
